reference: Use case: ads-marketing. Asset: clean architecture reference / final cinematic keyframe for an alternate CGC commercial glazing concept film titled IN PLAIN SIGHT. Generate ONE photorealistic architectural photograph, landscape 16:9, of a beautiful but believable modern Southern California tenant-improvement office. An empty rectangular conference room is enclosed by full-height clear frameless glass walls in the middle-right of a bright open office; thin graphite ceiling channels and a narrow graphite floor channel, discrete real door hardware, one closed stationary glass door at the far short end. Three glass faces are legible from this exterior three-quarter viewpoint. A pale oak rectangular meeting table and exactly six graphite upholstered chairs (three along each long side), no chairs at the ends. Pale gray terrazzo floor continues through the enclosure, white square structural columns outside the enclosure, exposed white ceiling beams and restrained black linear lights. Large exterior office windows at left admit soft late-morning daylight and a restrained tree/sky reflection onto glass. Clean white, graphite and soft steel-blue material palette. Frame the entire glass room and adjacent corridor with straight verticals and coherent room proportions, eye-level approximately 35mm architectural photography, beautiful natural light and subtle accurate reflection/transmission, professional editorial photography rather than CGI. The image should communicate a room defined by nearly invisible glass while keeping long open sightlines. No people, laptops, screens, signs, branding, lettering, numbers, borders, collage, impossible floating glass or decorative glowing edges. This is clearly an illustrative architectural concept, not a photograph of a completed CGC project.
storyboard: Use case: ads-marketing. Create a polished PHOTOREALISTIC SIX-FRAME STORYBOARD for a new commercial glazing concept film titled IN PLAIN SIGHT. Use the attached image as the architectural continuity reference, not as a page to reproduce. The story concerns an almost-invisible glass conference enclosure revealed by camera parallax. The glass is already installed in every frame: no wall disappearing, construction morph, opening doors, people, tools or fantasy effects. The same rectangular glass conference room, pale oak table, SIX graphite chairs inside (three per long side), narrow graphite top and bottom channels, stationary far-end glass door, pale gray terrazzo, white columns, exposed white ceiling beams, black linear lights and exterior windows with trees at LEFT must stay consistent across shots. Do not invent another building or different table. White/graphite/steel-blue palette, soft late-morning daylight. Premium real architectural photography with coherent reflection/transmission, straight verticals and realistic materials. Design a tall portrait white-paper board with TWO COLUMNS and THREE ROWS, exactly SIX cinematic landscape 16:9 images with crisp white gutters. Title IN PLAIN SIGHT at top in bold graphite sans-serif, small subtitle 16 SECOND CONCEPT FILM / SIX SHOTS. Only 01 through 06 small numbers beneath the frames; no prose, logos or branding. FRAME 01 straight-on medium view looking through a nearly reflection-free existing glass wall at the meeting table; glass channels mostly outside crop, so the room initially feels open. FRAME 02 exterior three-quarter closer view where a sharp glass corner and thin floor channel become visible in the foreground; the same table behind clear glass makes the boundary legible. FRAME 03 low macro of that same glass wall meeting its narrow graphite floor channel, pale terrazzo continuous on both sides; beautiful precise detail, real thin edge, no glowing outline. FRAME 04 long oblique exterior corridor view along the conference glass, with the left-side windows and tree reflections gently visible in the pane while the table is still transmitted through it; strong real near/far depth. FRAME 05 interior viewpoint from inside this same conference room, looking outward through stationary clear glazing into the bright open office; a small portion of the same oak table is in foreground and glass office lines remain stable. FRAME 06 wide composed exterior three-quarter reveal of the complete glass enclosure and corridor, matching the supplied reference; same table/chair count, channels, columns, windows and lighting. The visual story is SPACE LOOKS OPEN / A CAMERA SHIFT REVEALS THE GLASS / PRECISE EDGE DETAIL / REFLECTION EXPLAINS THE BOUNDARY / THE VIEW STAYS OPEN / A COMPLETE ROOM IN PLAIN SIGHT. This is an illustrative concept for CGC, not actual completed contractor work. Make the images art-directed and distinct in scale, not six near-identical crops.
